newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Standard rate cut reflects end of govt levy.
newsitem.headline: Standard rate cut reflects end of govt levy.

text.p: South Africa's Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd said on Wednesday its decision to cut prime lending rate to 19.25 percent from 19.50, effective October 1, reflected the removal of the Financial Services Levy.

The levy was introduced by the government as a surrogate for value added tax when VAT was introduced in 1991, the bank said in a statement. At that time banks increased prime by 0.25 percent to recover this cost.
Now the levy is being scrapped following the imposition of VAT on financial services from October 1.
Standard Bank chief executive Mike Vosloo said the new system of imposing VAT on financial services would be more equitable because VAT charges would be directly related to actual service usage.
"We are pleased to be able to alleviate some pressure on our borrowers," he said.
